profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility EWR12, at 365 South Randolphville Road, Piscataway Township, NJ 08854. Digital Realty's own property listing confirms this address as EWR12, but this session's fetch did not return a confirmed square footage figure for it specifically.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's New York/New Jersey metro footprint, which spans historic Manhattan carrier hotels and a cluster of suburban New Jersey buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township, coded EWR10 through EWR21 on the company's own metro listing. Digital Realty markets these properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and Silicon Valley, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. PSE&G serves most of the central New Jersey data center market.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than by individual building, and this pattern is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, not specific to this entry.

Con Edison serves most of Manhattan, and PSE&G serves most of northern New Jersey. reading.body:
The critical power capacity of this facility remains unconfirmed despite multiple source attempts, illustrating a persistent gap in public data for major data center infrastructure.

Digital Realty operates EWR12 as part of a multi-building campus across New Jersey's Piscataway Township, Clifton, and Weehawken. The facility sits in the New York metropolitan region, where proximity to power infrastructure and existing urban density shape data center placement. The company's naming convention ties buildings to Newark airport code EWR, suggesting portfolio organization around transportation and utility corridors rather than individual facility logic.

The absence of tier-one confirmation for individual building capacity is significant. Unlike some operators, Digital Realty does not publish per-facility megawatt specifications on accessible sources, even as sites like datacenterHawk and UPSTACK Marketplace attempt to catalog supply. This opacity compounds the challenge of mapping total regional compute power to actual electrical demand and grid strain, which are essential inputs for understanding whether capacity constraints are technical or informational.

The New Jersey campus represents material infrastructure, but this record cannot answer whether EWR12 is a modular 5 MW box or a 100+ MW hyperscaler core. Address confirmation shows the site exists. Power availability in its location cannot be derived from that fact alone.
